text.content:
This is the reference for the Automation column of the data workbooks (data/*.xlsx), written for the person typing in the cell. The Foundry system reads the cell with one parser (foundry/starwrought/module/rules/) at build time and in play, so what is written here is what the system does. Every change to a rule kind, a tag, a keyword or a vocabulary updates this document in the same commit (CLAUDE.md, standing rule, 2026-11-05), and the build fails when a kind, a tag, a component or a keyword the system knows is not named here. In Foundry the same text is the STARWROUGHT Automation Grammar journal in the Rules compendium, one page per section, opened by the Grammar button beside any Automation panel and the sheet's custom effects.

The grammar has the shape of Fantasy Grounds' Pathfinder 2 automation, which Mike asked for by name (2026-11-05: "I REALLY, REALLY like the FantasyGrounds effects automation ... can we use syntax substantially similar to this"), and since 0.17.0 every line of a cell is blocks in square brackets, as FG's PC feature automation is (Mike: "shouldn't ALL of those be enclosed in Brackets?"):

  • Feature blocks: what owning the Talent does to the character. [TRAIT Human][SIZE Medium][SPEED 6][VIGOR 8], [Acrobatics trained], [MANEUVER Steady the Line].
  • Effect blocks, [EFFECT ...]: what the Talent does to a roll, a tag then components separated by semicolons, FG's own wrapper for an effect inside a feature. [EFFECT CHECK: 1 condition, aid; IF: RANK(Origin >= trained)], [EFFECT IMMUNE: prone; LIMIT: encounter].
[TRAIT Human][SIZE Medium][SPEED 6][VIGOR 8]
[EFFECT CHECK: 1 condition, aid; IF: RANK(Origin >= trained)]
[EFFECT DEF: 1 situation, guard; IFT: BLOW; FOR: self+allies 0; IF: ALLIES(>=1, 0)]
[MANEUVER Oathbound]

Every block the cell reads, one example each. Case never matters.

writeit meanssection
[TRAIT Human]the character has the trait2
[SIZE Medium]the body's Size2
[SPEED 6], [SPEED +1]Speed in feet per Move, or an adjustment to it2
[VIGOR 8], [VIGOR opening 12]Vigor per level; a Calling's Opening Vigor2
[SENSES Low-light vision]a sense2
[LANGUAGE Common, Serrovine]languages known2
[Acrobatics trained], [Lore trained]a Trained Root at creation, one directed Talent Point2
[POINT Skill], [POINT 2 Skill different]Talent Points at creation, by scope2
[MANEUVER Steady the Line]the Maneuver of that name is the character's2
[TALENT Weapon Familiarity]a Talent handed over free2
[CHOICE Weapon Group]a pick the Talent demands at creation2
[AURA 15 allies]a ring on the map, preview-only until shown2
[AURA 15 allies; DEF: 1 situation; IF: SEEN]a ring that carries its effect: the ring is the effect's FOR2
[REQUIRES prone or supine]on a Maneuver's own row: what the Maneuver needs before it can be used; the Maneuvers tab lists the row only while it holds2
[EFFECT CHECK: 1 condition, aid]a bonus to checks of a Constellation or Maneuver (none named: every check)3
[EFFECT ATK: 1 condition]a bonus to every Strike and Cast3
[EFFECT DEF: 1 situation, guard]a bonus to a Defense (none named: all four)3
[EFFECT INIT: 1 situation]a bonus to Initiative3
[EFFECT SPEED: 1 situation]feet on a Move3
[EFFECT IMMUNE: prone], [EFFECT IMMUNE: expose]a Condition, or an Expose, does not land3
[EFFECT MARK: enemies]using it names one creature3
[EFFECT REROLL: diplomacy]the card of a matching roll offers the die again3
[EFFECT IGNORE: terrain, mud]difficult terrain of those kinds costs nothing3
[EFFECT USE: Presence, Origin, aid]a check made from that Maneuver may be rolled with that Attribute and that Constellation's Proficiency Bonus in place of its own (same keeps a term)3
[EFFECT GIVE: 1 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(success)]on a Maneuver's own row: that result of its check gives another character a bonus (or a penalty) on its next roll with a Constellation, named when it is given (chosen) or by the line3
[EFFECT ALTER: Aid.critical-failure; VALUE: nothing]on a Talent: one property of that Maneuver is changed (a result to nothing, a window with Aid.beneficial-duration, its movement to a Step with Move Together.movement; VALUE: step, or how often it may be used with Pay It Forward.limit; VALUE: round)3
[EFFECT PERMIT: move; FOR: allies 0; LIMIT: round]on a Maneuver's own row: using it lets the adjacent ally you target make one Move now, outside its Opportunity, once a round3
[EFFECT SUBORDINATE: Aid; LIMIT: encounter]on a Maneuver's own row: using it performs that Maneuver as part of it, at this row's own cost and never the other's (the Subordinate Maneuver rule)3
; UNTIL: recipient opportunity 2... a GIVE's window: giver opportunity (the default), recipient opportunity <N>, encounter3
; VALUE: nothing... what an ALTER's property becomes3
; IF: RANK(Origin >= trained)... while the owner's rank is at least that3
; IF: RANK(roll = untrained)... while the rank the roll is made at is that (the borrowed Constellation's when a USE stands; on a USE line itself, the check's own rank before the swap)3
; IF: SEEN... for a recipient who can see the owner3
; IF: ALLIES(>=1, 0)... while that many allies stand within the range (ENEMIES, ALL)3
; IF: CLAIM(when trading)... when the player says so (a checkbox in the roll dialog, or Apply to next roll)3
; IF: RESULT(critical failure)... on that degree (REROLL and GIVE only)3
; IF: EFFECT(Aid, used)... once a roll of yours at your own Opportunity has used up a bonus another creature's Aid gave you (SUBORDINATE only)3
; IFT: TRAIT(Fear)... against an attack carrying the trait3
; IFT: MARKED... against the creature the MARK named3
; IFT: BLOW (BLAST, BLIGHT, BEGUILEMENT, MELEE, RANGED)... against that Threat, or a Blow by its reach3
; IFT: CHECK(intimidation)... against a check of that Constellation read on this Defense3
; FOR: allies 15... given to allies within 15 ft (self, enemies, all, self+allies)3
; LIMIT: round, ; LIMIT: encounter... the first time each round, or each encounter3

• A line is one or more blocks in square brackets. A cell may hold any number of lines; a [EFFECT ...] block is best on a line of its own, for reading.
  • A blank line is nothing. A line beginning with # is a comment.
  • **N/A means the row needs no automation** (0.26.1). Type it alone in the cell of a Talent or a Maneuver you have looked at and decided needs none. It is no rule and no error: the pipeline treats the cell as empty, the Foundry Item's Automation box stays empty, and the red-cell tool never paints it and counts it apart, so a blank cell is one you have not reached yet and an N/A cell is one you have. n/a, NA, N.A., None and a lone dash read the same, with or without brackets ([N/A]). It is the whole line: N/A inside a block ([EFFECT N/A]) is a mistyped effect and is still refused. A cell that says N/A and also carries rules is warned about, and the rules are what the build uses.
  • Case does not matter anywhere: [effect check: 1 Condition, Aid], [trait human] and IF: rank(ORIGIN >= Trained) all read.
  • Spaces are free around commas, colons and semicolons. One trailing period inside a block is tolerated.
  • Names are the book's: Constellations (Guard, Stealth, Elementalism), Maneuvers (Aid, Steady the Line), Conditions (prone), Threats (BLOW), ranks (trained), Attributes (presence). A Maneuver's cost glyphs are ignored (Aid and Aid ❶ are one name). The slug form (armored-fighting) reads too.
  • Feet are a number with ft attached or not: 15, 15ft, 15 ft. 0 means adjacent.
  • A block ends at the first ] outside parentheses (0.18.1): a CLAIM(...) text may say "[per the table]" and the block runs on to its own ]. Outside a condition's parentheses nothing a block carries contains one.

A line the parser cannot read fails the release build (node assets/build_all.mjs) with the Constellation, the Talent, the line number and what is wrong, before anything is written to the pack sources. The content loop is lenient (sync_content.cmd, node assets/build_all.mjs --content; since 2026-11-07): the same line is listed under an AUTOMATION ERRORS banner and stored on its Item as an error, which the Item sheet's Automation panel shows in red and the engine skips, exactly as a GM's wrongly edited textarea line is treated in an open world; the lines that did read on the same cell are rules as usual. So a sheet half-authored (a [Medicine trained] before the Medicine sheet exists) still builds, and the release stops until it is mended. Nothing is ever thrown at the table over a cell.

Red cells in the workbooks. python assets/highlight_automation.py (2026-11-08) paints every cell this parser cannot read solid red in data/*.xlsx, with a cell comment giving the message for each line and why: mis-typed (the nearest name offered when one is close), no kind yet (nothing in this document reads what the line asks), or not yet readable (the cell is right, but the sheet it names is not in its _Tree Index, or the workbook it names is one the converter does not read). Fix the cell and run it again and its red goes. automation-cells-report.md in the project root lists the red cells and the kinds they ask for.

A bare effect line in a cell is refused (since 0.18.0; it read with a warning in 0.17.0). IMMUNE: prone; LIMIT: encounter on a line of its own, without the [EFFECT ...] wrapper, is one error quoting the block to write. The bare line is the form of the sheet's custom effects alone (section 6), as FG's Character Effects field takes the bare string.

The 0.13.0 form is refused since 0.17.0. A line in the old operator shape (bonus: +1, Condition, Aid, IF(Origin=Trained), grant: 1, Calling, aura: 15ft, allies, VISIBLE, prevent: Prone, ONCE(encounter), or a mark:, reroll: or ignore: line carrying IF(...)-style operators) is one error naming this document; section 9 maps each old operator to its component. The 0.10.0 prose form (bonus: +1 Condition to Aid if Human is Expert) stays refused.

pages.name: Feature lines: what owning the Talent does

text.content:
A feature line is one or more blocks in square brackets, [KEYWORD data], any number on a line. Each block is one rule.

blockmeansstored kind
[TRAIT Human]the character has the trait (the Ancestry's on its Root; any Talent may add one)trait
[SIZE Medium]the body's Size: Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, Gargantuansize
[SPEED 6]Speed in feet per Move; [SPEED +1] or [SPEED -1] adjusts itspeed
[VIGOR 8]Vigor per level (the Ancestry's); [VIGOR opening 12] a Calling's Opening Vigorvigor
[SENSES Low-light vision]a sense, added to the listsense
[LANGUAGE Common, Serrovine]languages known, comma separatedlanguage
[Acrobatics trained]a Trained Root in that Constellation at creation, FG's own form for a proficiency: one directed Talent Point that buys the Root (a Background's, a Calling's). [Lore trained] lets the player name the Lore. Only trained reads: nothing grants a higher rank at creationgrant
[POINT Skill]a Talent Point at creation, by scope: Opening (a Root of a Constellation not yet opened), Calling, Skill (a Lore included), Lore, Defense, Combat Style, Comet (anywhere you qualify); [POINT 2 Skill different] is two points in different Constellationsgrant
[MANEUVER Steady the Line]the Maneuver of that name, a row of data/maneuvers.xlsx, is the character's: copied onto the sheet when the Talent lands, listed under "From your Talents", used from there, gone with the Talent. The row's own Cost and Automation are the Maneuver'smaneuver
[TALENT Weapon Familiarity]a Talent handed over free, no point spent (the Free Talent column's successor)talent
[CHOICE Weapon Group]a build-time pick the Talent demands (the Choice column's successor)choice
[AURA 15 allies]the ring on the map: range in feet, whom it is about (allies, enemies, all). Every ring is preview-only until its owner shows it from the Auras window (0.17.0; the old visible word is refused)aura
[AURA 15 allies; DEF: 1 situation; IF: SEEN; IFT: TRAIT(Fear); LIMIT: round]the ring carrying its effect (0.18.0): after the semicolon, one effect line (section 3) whose FOR is the ring, so "15 feet, allies" is said once; a FOR: inside the block is refused. Stored as two rules, the ring and the effect. A second effect on the same ring is a second block with the same range and audience, drawn once; two rings on one Talent draw the firstaura, and the effect's kind
[REQUIRES prone or supine]on a Maneuver's own row: what the Maneuver needs before it can be used (0.28.0). The Maneuvers tab lists the row only while every block on it holds; or inside a block gives alternatives, not turns a word round, and a second block is a condition that must also hold. The words are in section 4requires
[EFFECT ...]an effect block: section 3the tag's kind

The chassis is written on the Root. The Human's [TRAIT Human][SIZE Medium][SPEED 6][VIGOR 8] and the Serrovanian's [LANGUAGE Common, Serrovine] are the authoring of the Ancestry's and the Culture's facts since 0.16.0; the _Tree Index columns Vigor, Size, Speed, Senses, Traits and Languages, the Callings' Skills column and the roster's Opening Vigor column are retired, read one release with a warning, and a disagreement between a column and the Root's block fails the build. The pipeline (assets/parse_rules.mjs) carries the Root's blocks into the roster records the web app, the compendium docx and the Foundry build read, so every consumer sees one source.

**@Maneuver[Name] in an Effect cell.** A Talent that grants a Maneuver need not repeat the Maneuver's text: @Maneuver[Oathbound] in its Effect is replaced, wherever the Effect prints (the web app, the docx, the Talent Item, the wizard's card), by the Maneuver's block: its name and cost, Trigger, Requirements and Effect from the row. A name that is no row fails the build.

pages.name: Effect blocks: what the Talent does to a roll

text.content:
[EFFECT TAG: <value> <type>, <descriptor>; <component>; <component> ...]

The tag names what is modified. A modifier tag (CHECK, ATK, DEF, INIT, SPEED, GIVE) takes a signed whole number and a bonus type (situation, condition or gear, the book's three; FG's [bonus]), then at most one descriptor after a comma (GIVE exactly one). The other tags (IMMUNE, MARK, REROLL, IGNORE, USE, ALTER, PERMIT, SUBORDINATE) take descriptors alone; USE takes exactly three and ALTER, PERMIT and SUBORDINATE exactly one, and never a value or a type. No bonus is untyped.

tagmodifiesdescriptorstored kind
CHECK: 2 condition, diplomacychecks of a Constellation or made from a Maneuver (CHECK: 1 condition, aid); with no descriptor every check (an Initiative rolled with a Constellation is a check in it, ruling 111)a Constellation or a Maneuver by name; a Lore is refusedbonus
ATK: 1 conditionevery Strike and Castnonebonus
DEF: 1 situation, guarda Defense's roll and Threshold; with no descriptor all fourevade, guard, endure, awarenessbonus
INIT: 1 situationInitiativenonebonus
SPEED: 1 situationfeet on a Move (not a Step, a Rush or a Leap)nonebonus
IMMUNE: pronethe Condition does not land; IMMUNE: expose a Zone a Stop would Expose stays closed (FG's own IMMUNE: [condition])a Condition by name, or exposeprevent
MARK: enemiesusing the Talent or Maneuver names one creature, the player's target, until the encounter ends; enemies or allwho may be namedmark
REROLL: diplomacythe card of a matching roll offers to throw the die again; no descriptor means any checka Constellationreroll
IGNORE: terrain, mud, deckingdifficult terrain of those kinds costs nothing; IGNORE: terrain alone every kindterrain, then kindsignore
USE: Presence, Origin, aidthe two base terms of a check made from a Maneuver's own Item, written USE: <Attribute>, <Constellation>, <Maneuver>: the Attribute Bonus and the Proficiency Bonus are the named Attribute's and the named Constellation's in place of the check's own, offered in the roll dialog; nothing else on the roll changes (0.21.0)exactly three: an Attribute or same, a Constellation or same, then a Maneuver by namesubstitute
GIVE: 1 situation, chosenwhat a result of this Maneuver's check gives ANOTHER character: a bonus or penalty on that character's next roll with a Constellation. Written on the Maneuver's own row, one line for each degree that gives something, each with IF: RESULT(<degree>) (0.22.0)exactly one: chosen (the Constellation is named when the result is given) or a Constellation by namegive
ALTER: Aid.critical-failureone property of a Maneuver, changed by a Talent: ALTER: <Maneuver>.<property>; VALUE: <value>. The properties read are in the Property vocabulary below (0.22.0; movement since 0.24.0, limit since 0.25.0)exactly one: the Maneuver by name, a dot, the propertyalter
PERMIT: moveusing this Maneuver lets the creature you target make one Move now, outside its Opportunity, paying for it itself; your own next drag is the Maneuver's Move, already paid. Written on the Maneuver's own row, with FOR: saying who may be permitted and how near (FOR: allies 0 is an adjacent ally) and LIMIT: its Frequency (0.24.0)exactly one: what is permitted (move)permit
SUBORDINATE: Aidusing this Maneuver performs the named Maneuver as part of it. The named Maneuver keeps its own check, results and requirements; its own cost is never charged, and the cost printed on THIS row is the only one paid (the Subordinate Maneuver rule, below). Written on the Maneuver's own row, with IF: EFFECT(<name>, used) its trigger when it has one and LIMIT: its Frequency (0.25.0)exactly one: the Maneuver performed, by namesubordinate

The Subordinate Maneuver rule (Mike, 2026-11-15; ruling 245). When a Maneuver says to perform another Maneuver as part of it, the other is done at the first Maneuver's listed cost: it costs no additional actions, unless the row says otherwise. So an Aid made as part of Pay It Forward ⓿ costs nothing, whatever Aid's own row prints. Everything else about the subordinate Maneuver stands: its check, its results, its requirements. No row says otherwise yet, so the grammar has no word for an extra cost; one comes with the first row that charges it.

A bonus to a Constellation moves its Threshold as well as its roll (section 7). A bonus to a Maneuver is applied when the roll is made from that Maneuver's Item and otherwise offered unticked in the roll dialog ("Humanity: Aid"; ruling 122). A USE is offered in the roll dialog too, but only when the roll is made from the Maneuver's own Item and never on another check: a checkbox naming the two pairs ("Cooperative Instinct: Presence and Origin (Trained) in place of Wits and Crafting (Untrained)") with the signed difference in the total beside it, ticked by default when the swapped total is strictly higher (rulings 218 and 219; section 4, substitute).

Components follow the tag, each after a semicolon:

componentmeans
IF: <condition>about the owner, or the roll itself
IFT: <condition>about the other party: the attacker you answer, the defender your Strike meets, the attack itself
FOR: allies 15who receives it: self (the default), allies, enemies, all, self+allies, within that range of the owner; FOR: self takes no range
LIMIT: roundthe first time it would apply to each recipient in a round, and not again until the next round
LIMIT: encounterthe first time in an encounter, and not again until the next. Outside an encounter either applies every time, said on the card
UNTIL: recipient opportunity 2after GIVE alone: the window in which the result may be used (the Window vocabulary below). With none, giver opportunity. Every other tag refuses it by name
VALUE: nothingafter ALTER alone: what the property becomes, nothing for a result and a window for a duration (VALUE: recipient opportunity 2). Every other tag refuses it by name

Both IF: and IFT: accept every condition (FG's own users mix them); the idiomatic prefix is the one in the table. Several IF:/IFT: components on one line must all hold.

conditionmeansidiom
RANK(Origin >= trained)the owner's rank in that Constellation: =, >= or <=; Origin is the pooled Ancestry, Bloodline and Culture rank; a group (a Combat Style, a magical specialty) is refused naming its parentIF:
RANK(roll = untrained)the rank the roll is made at, Handling included (roll is the reserved word): the borrowed Constellation's when a USE stands (ruling 217); on a USE line itself, the check's own rank, before any swapIF:
SEENthe recipient can see you: a straight line from their token's centre to yours crosses no sight-blocking wall, they are not Blinded, your token is not hidden nor you Hidden or Undetected (ruling 170)IF:
ALLIES(>=1, 0)how many allies stand within the range of the owner; >=, <=, =, >, <IF:
ENEMIES(>=2, 15)how many enemies stand within the rangeIF:
ALL(>=3, 5)how many creatures of either side stand within the rangeIF:
CLAIM(when trading)the player decides: the bonus is a checkbox in the roll dialog with these words as its hint, unticked; the Effects tab's "Apply to next roll" and the pin on the Talent's row arm it for the next roll (ruling 174)IF:
RESULT(critical failure)the roll's degree: critical success, success, failure, critical failure. Only REROLL (the degree that offers the die again) and GIVE (the degree that gives the result) read itIF:
EFFECT(Aid, used)a named Effect (0.25.0, step one of two): a roll of yours, made at your own Opportunity that is still running, has used up the Effect of that name, and it was a bonus another creature gave you. The name is the Maneuver whose result it was. Only SUBORDINATE reads it. The plain EFFECT(<name>) (an Effect you hold now) and IFT: EFFECT(...) (one on the other party) are refused as not read yet: they come with the named Effects a Maneuver can give a targetIF:
TRAIT(Fear)the attack answered carries the trait (a weapon's, an adversary attack's or a spell Talent's), matched on its first word; the build warns when nothing shipping carries it (ruling 171)IFT:
MARKEDthe other party is the creature this Talent's or Maneuver's MARK named (FG's IFT: CUSTOM(Hunt Prey))IFT:
BLOWthe Threat answered is a Blow (a weapon's Strike, an adversary's attack row)IFT:
BLASTthe Threat answered is a BlastIFT:
BLIGHTthe Threat answered is a BlightIFT:
BEGUILEMENTthe Threat answered is a BeguilementIFT:
MELEEa Blow that reached by handIFT:
RANGEDa Blow that reached by a missile or a throwIFT:
CHECK(intimidation)the check read against this Defense rolls that Constellation (a character's Demoralize against your Guard reads your live Threshold, ruling 179)IFT:

Who. Allies are tokens of the same disposition as the owner on the scene, as the Support rule counts them: never a party token, a hidden token, or a Dying, unconscious or dead body. Enemies are tokens of the opposite disposition. all is everyone but the owner. Ranges are measured edge to edge in feet; 0 is adjacency.

Rank. untrained, trained, expert, master, legendary.

Attribute. might, agility, wits, presence: the first descriptor of USE. The word same stands there, or in the second descriptor, for a term the check keeps: it means "the term this check would use without this line".

Window (0.22.0). How long a result a Maneuver gave may be used, after UNTIL: on a GIVE line and after VALUE: on an ALTER of a duration. giver opportunity is until the giver's next Opportunity begins, and is what a GIVE has when it says nothing; giver opportunity 2 waits for the second. recipient opportunity 2 runs through the END of the recipient's second upcoming Opportunity (an Opportunity already running when the result is given is not counted). encounter is until the encounter ends. Every window also ends with the encounter, and outside an encounter a result lasts until it is used, replaced or removed.

Property (0.22.0). What an ALTER may change of the results a Maneuver gives, after the dot: duration (every result's window), beneficial-duration (the window of the results that give a bonus, so a penalty keeps its own), and the four results by degree, critical-success, success, failure, critical-failure, each of which is changed to nothing. Since 0.24.0 one more, which is not about what the Maneuver gives: movement, changed to step, so that a drag within half Speed made as part of the Maneuver is a Step for everyone who moves in it (Coordinated Footwork, of Move Together). Since 0.25.0 another: limit, changed to round or encounter, which replaces the LIMIT: on the Maneuver's own row (Reciprocal Effort, of Pay It Forward: once a round in place of once an encounter); it never adds a use, and a row with no LIMIT: stays unlimited. Any other property is refused as not read yet. Where two lines change one Maneuver, beneficial-duration stands over duration in either order, and of two changes to one property the later stands.

Named Effect (0.25.0, step one). Mike, 2026-11-15, after Fantasy Grounds: "using a Maneuver can grant a custom Effect on a target (with a specific duration), and other modifiers/effects can be applied IF that custom Effect field is on the target." Built in two steps by his choice. Step one is an Effect the SYSTEM leaves: when a roll of yours uses up a bonus another creature's Maneuver gave you, at your own Opportunity, you hold an Effect named for that result with "(used)" after it (Aid from Wren (used)) until that Opportunity ends, listed on the Effects tab under Pending results. IF: EFFECT(<Maneuver>, used) reads it. A penalty a roll swallowed, a roll on another fighter's Opportunity, an Initiative, and a result the GM binned or whose window closed leave nothing. Step two, not built: a Maneuver that puts a named Effect on its target for a duration, and CHECK, DEF and ATK lines reading IF: EFFECT(<name>) on the owner and IFT: EFFECT(<name>) on the other party.

Trait. Any word; the attack's traits are the weapon's Traits column, the adversary attack Item's Traits, or the spell Talent's Traits column on its tree sheet.

Terrain kind. The names of the hand-kept terrainKinds block of assets/roster.json (0.18.0; today mud, shallow water, decking, loose stone, rubble, undergrowth, snow, ice, sand, other), which is also the Difficult terrain region behavior's dropdown, so the words in a cell and on the map are one vocabulary; a row added to the block is a kind a cell may name.

pages.name: The kinds, by their stored names

text.content:
The sheet's As read list and the build's messages name a rule by its kind. These are the words, each with the blocks that make it.

bonus

A typed bonus or penalty to a roll, and to the Threshold that roll's Constellation presents. Made by [EFFECT CHECK: ...], ATK, DEF, INIT and SPEED. Every component applies.

prevent

An effect does not land: a Condition, or an Expose. Made by [EFFECT IMMUNE: ...]. Takes every component but CLAIM. With FOR the prevention reaches others; when the carrier is a Reaction (↺ in its cost) it is offered as that Reaction where the effect would land, and the owner pays its cost.

mark

Using the Talent or Maneuver names one creature. Made by [EFFECT MARK: ...]. Takes IF: RANK(...) alone.

reroll

The card of a matching roll offers to throw the die again, at the cost in the carrier's name. Made by [EFFECT REROLL: ...]. Takes IF: RANK(...) and IF: RESULT(...).

ignore

Difficult terrain of named kinds costs nothing. Made by [EFFECT IGNORE: ...]. Takes IF: RANK(...) alone.

substitute

A check made with another Attribute and another Constellation's Proficiency Bonus (0.21.0; rulings 215 to 222). Made by [EFFECT USE: ...]. It is for a Talent such as Cooperative Instinct (Mike, 2026-11-10: "When you Aid, you may use Presence + Origin proficiency in place of the Attribute and proficiency normally used for that Aid check"; and his generalisation: "Replacing the Constellation AND the Attribute bonus for a check with something else").

[EFFECT USE: <Attribute>, <Constellation>, <Maneuver>]

[EFFECT USE: Presence, Origin, aid]        Cooperative Instinct
[EFFECT USE: same, Origin, aid]            the Proficiency Bonus alone; the check keeps its Attribute
[EFFECT USE: Presence, same, aid]          the Attribute alone
[EFFECT USE: Presence, Origin, aid; IF: RANK(Origin >= expert); LIMIT: encounter]

Exactly three descriptors, in this order (ruling 215):

  • The Attribute the check is made with: might, agility, wits or presence, or same.
  • The Constellation whose Proficiency Bonus is borrowed, by the name the trees print: Origin, a Skill or a Defense, or same. A Maneuver and a Lore are refused, a group is refused naming its parent (as RANK does), and so is a rank word or a number: a flat Proficiency Bonus is not read yet.
  • The Maneuver whose check is swapped, by the name the action sheets print (aid; its cost glyphs are ignored). A Constellation, a Defense, a scope word (checks), a Lore and same are refused: a USE never means every check (ruling 219).

same is "the term this check would use without this line". same, same swaps nothing and is refused. The likely slips have messages of their own (section 8): a + between the two terms, as the Talent's prose has it; a value and a type; two descriptors; four.

Takes IF: RANK(...) and LIMIT: alone. On a USE line RANK(roll ...) is the check's own rank, before any swap. Every other component is refused by name (FOR, IF: SEEN, the counts, IF: CLAIM(...), IF: RESULT(...), and every condition about the other party: IFT: TRAIT(...), IFT: MARKED, a Threat, IFT: CHECK(...)), and a USE after the ring of an [AURA ...] block is refused in its own words: a substitution is the owner's own roll.

As read: may use Presence + Origin proficiency on checks to Aid; with one term kept, may use Origin proficiency on checks to Aid or may use Presence on checks to Aid. The components follow as on any line (..., while Origin is at least Expert, once each encounter), a RANK(roll ...) as while the check's own rank is Untrained.

In play:

  • It replaces the two base terms and nothing else (ruling 216): the Attribute Bonus and the Proficiency Bonus. The roll stays a check in its own Constellation, so the Flare preselection, Load Strain on Stealth, bonuses to that Constellation, rerolls and the road-roll memory are untouched.
  • The rank recorded is the rank rolled (ruling 217): the borrowed Constellation's when a swap stands. Every other rule's IF: RANK(roll ...) reads that rank, and the card prints it; Aid's "master with the check you attempted" is read there.
  • Offered, and only from the Maneuver's own Item (rulings 218 and 219; Mike: "Only from Aid"). A check made from the Maneuver's Item shows a checkbox in the roll dialog, "Cooperative Instinct: Presence and Origin (Trained) in place of Wits and Crafting (Untrained)", with the signed difference in the total beside it. A check made without that Item is offered nothing.
  • Ticked when it is better (ruling 218; Mike: "ticking it by default when it is a better pair"). Better is judged on the whole assembled total, not on the two base numbers, because another rule may read the rank: the box is ticked only when the swapped total is strictly higher, and a tie or a loss is offered unticked. One swap stands on a roll. With no dialog (a Shift-click) the default applies.
  • The card says so: "Cooperative Instinct: Presence and Origin (Trained) in place of Wits and Crafting (Untrained)." The card keeps the record in its flags (flags.starwrought.substituted, beside the Attribute rolled, flags.starwrought.attribute, and the rank rolled, flags.starwrought.rank). In the Relevant Check picker a row whose number includes a swap is marked with an asterisk, and one hint line under the list names the Talent.
  • Checks only, characters only (ruling 220): never a Strike, a Cast, a Defense roll, a Threshold read or an Initiative; an adversary rolls flat.
  • A limit is spent by the swap that is rolled (ruling 221): a LIMIT: is never spent by a swap that was offered and left unticked.
  • On / Skip / Off on the Effects tab switch the line like any effect line (section 6), and Skip or Off is how a swap is declined on a roll with no dialog.

give

What a result of a Maneuver's check gives another character (0.22.0; rulings 223 to 230). Made by [EFFECT GIVE: ...], and written on the Maneuver's own row, because it is the Maneuver's own result. It is for Aid (PHB v4.24): a Success gives the ally a +1 Situation bonus, a Critical Success +2 (+3 "if you're a master with the check you attempted", +4 if legendary), a Critical Failure a -1 Situation penalty. Through 0.21.0 that was prose on the card, applied by hand.

[EFFECT GIVE: <value> <type>, chosen | <Constellation>; IF: RESULT(<degree>); IF: RANK(...); UNTIL: <window>]

[EFFECT GIVE: 2 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: RANK(roll <= expert)]
[EFFECT GIVE: 3 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: RANK(roll = master)]
[EFFECT GIVE: 4 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: RANK(roll = legendary)]
[EFFECT GIVE: 1 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(success)]
[EFFECT GIVE: -1 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical failure)]        Aid's row, whole
  • The value and the type, as on any modifier tag: a signed whole number, then situation, condition or gear. A negative value is a penalty.
  • One descriptor: chosen, or a Constellation by name. chosen means the Constellation is named when the result is given, opening on the one the giver rolled (Mike, 2026-11-14: "Named separately"); a named Constellation fixes it. A Maneuver, a Lore, a group and a scope word are refused (a Lore is reached through chosen).
  • **Exactly one IF: RESULT(<degree>)** says which result gives it (ruling 223). One line for each degree that gives something; a degree with no line gives nothing.
  • **IF: RANK(...)** chooses between lines for one degree: the owner's rank in a Constellation, or RANK(roll ...), the rank ROLLED (ruling 217), which is how "a master with the check you attempted" is written. The first line that holds for a degree is its result, so order the lines for one degree from the narrowest condition to the widest.
  • **UNTIL: <window>** (section 3, Window). With none the window is giver opportunity.

Refused by name: FOR, IF: SEEN, the counts, IF: CLAIM(...), LIMIT, every condition about the other party, and a GIVE after the ring of an [AURA ...] block. A GIVE in a Talent's cell or on a custom effect row is refused in its own words: a Talent changes what a Maneuver gives with ALTER.

As read: gives a +1 Situation bonus to the next roll with the Constellation chosen, on a Success, until the giver's next Opportunity.

In play (rulings 226 to 229):

  • Nothing is given by the roll. The check's card carries the result of its degree, and for the giver's owner and the GM a button: Give Wren +1 to Crafting when the giver had one character targeted (one click), with Other... beside it, or Give the result... when nobody was targeted. Other and Give the result open a dialog: who, and for a chosen result which of that character's Constellations. Never automatic (Mike: "A button on the card").
  • Pressing it puts one line on the recipient's Effects tab, "Aid from Tess: +1 Situation bonus to the next Crafting roll, until Tess's next Opportunity", and posts a card that says the same. That card is the record: the button on the check card gives way to "Given to Wren: +1 Situation to Crafting" on every client.
  • One result of a Maneuver is pending on a character at a time. A new Aid result replaces the one pending, whoever gave it, and the give card says so.
  • The recipient's next roll with that Constellation carries it, and it is gone: a check, a Maneuver's check, an attack, a Defense roll, an Initiative. It prints on the card as "Aid from Tess +1". It is never part of a Threshold on the sheet, and reading a Threshold (an attack resolved against it) neither carries it nor uses it up.
  • Unused, it goes when its window closes, or with the encounter. The window is counted from the press of the button, so press it when the Aid is made. Outside an encounter a result lasts until it is used, replaced or removed, and a result given in one encounter is never applied in another.
  • Recipients are characters, and never the giver. An adversary rolls flat and holds no such line.
  • A check made against no Threshold has no degree, and its card says there is nothing to give.
  • A reroll gives its own result. The first card's table holds every degree, so the new card offers what its own degree gives, and the card that was thrown again gives nothing. A result already given from the first card stays with whoever got it.
  • One client writes it: the GM's when a GM is connected, else the recipient's own player's, so two presses of one card are served in turn and the second is told it was already given. With neither connected nothing is given and the presser is told.
  • A roll its roller may not read (a blind roll) shows that roller no button: the button's words would say the degree. The GM has it.
  • The tracker's own Initiative die does not read a pending result. Roll Initiative from the sheet, or from the party's grid, to use one.

alter

A Talent that changes one property of what a Maneuver gives (0.22.0; rulings 223 to 230). Made by [EFFECT ALTER: ...], in the shape Mike drafted in the cells of two Human Talents before the kind existed (2026-11-14): Patient Assistance ("the Situation bonus provided by your Aid lasts until the end of the recipient's second upcoming Opportunity") and Sure Assistance ("A critical failure on your Aid check grants no penalty to your ally").

[EFFECT ALTER: <Maneuver>.<property>; VALUE: <value>; IF: RANK(...)]

[EFFECT ALTER: Aid.beneficial-duration; VALUE: recipient opportunity 2]     Patient Assistance
[EFFECT ALTER: Aid.critical-failure; VALUE: nothing]                        Sure Assistance
[EFFECT ALTER: Aid.duration; VALUE: encounter]                              every result of Aid
[EFFECT ALTER: Move Together.movement; VALUE: step]                         Coordinated Footwork
[EFFECT ALTER: Pay It Forward.limit; VALUE: round]                          Reciprocal Effort
  • One descriptor: the Maneuver by the name the action sheets print, a dot, the property (section 3, Property). Case, spaces and a Maneuver's cost glyphs do not matter.
  • **VALUE:** says what the property becomes: a window for duration and beneficial-duration, the word nothing for a result, the word step for movement, round or encounter for limit. It is read after ALTER alone.
  • **limit** (0.25.0; ruling 250) is how often the Maneuver may be used, from Reciprocal Effort (Mike's draft: "You may use Pay It Forward once per round instead of once per encounter"). It REPLACES the LIMIT: on the Maneuver's own row and never adds a use, so a use is counted by the round in place of the encounter, and a row with no LIMIT: stays unlimited. Like movement it is read when the Maneuver is USED, by subordinate and permit alike, so Move Together's LIMIT: round can be altered the same way. Mike's drafted value, owner round, is told to write round: a limit is always its owner's.
  • **movement** (0.24.0; ruling 242) is the one property that is not about what the Maneuver gives. It is read when the Maneuver is USED, by the permit kind below: with it, a drag within half Speed made as part of that Maneuver is a Step (one action, nothing provoked, no difficult terrain), for the user and for the one permitted alike; a longer drag is still a Move. Mike's draft of the cell, VALUE: choose(Move, Step); APPLY: both-participants, is told the word and that APPLY: is no component: the Step is always for both, and it is a choice only in that a short drag is one.
  • **IF: RANK(...)**: the owner's rank, or RANK(roll ...), the rank rolled.

An ALTER changes one property and leaves the rest, so there is no PRESERVE:. It never touches the roll: a Critical Failure that gives nothing is still a Critical Failure, and still offers a Flare. A property not in the list is refused as not read yet, naming the ones that are, before the Maneuver is looked up, so a cell drafted for a later version says what is missing rather than what is misspelt. Refused by name: FOR, LIMIT, IF: CLAIM(...), IF: RESULT(...) (the property names the degree), every condition about the other party, UNTIL, and an ALTER after the ring of an [AURA ...] block.

As read: Aid's results that give a bonus last through the recipient's second upcoming Opportunity; Aid's Critical Failure gives nothing.

In play:

  • Read from everything the roller carries: a Talent, an owned Maneuver, a custom effect. The card of the Maneuver's check shows the changed result, and under its button "Changed by Patient Assistance".
  • A result changed to nothing shows no button and the note "Sure Assistance: a Critical Failure gives nothing", so the table can tell it from a degree that never gave anything.
  • **beneficial-duration reaches the results that give a bonus** (Mike: a Success and a Critical Success). A penalty keeps its own window (Mike: "Same window as a bonus", the window a bonus has without the Talent).
  • Two changes to one Maneuver. The more particular property stands over the general one, whichever line comes first: beneficial-duration over duration. Of two changes to ONE property the later line stands, and the card names only the Talent whose change it shows.
  • On / Skip / Off on the Effects tab, as any effect line (section 6). A Skip, and a custom effect that lasts the next roll, is spent only by a roll whose degree the line CHANGES: Sure Assistance set to Skip is not used up by a Success, and a change that altered nothing (a result another Talent had already emptied) is not used up at all. A reroll reads the first card's results, so a line the first die did not spend is spent by the reroll that lands on its degree. A movement line is read when its Maneuver is used: on Skip it is left out that once (the drags are plain Moves) and the Skip is spent by a use that counted, never by a refused use or one outside an encounter; Off is Off; a custom effect that lasts the next roll is used up the same way. A limit line is read the same way: on Skip the row's own limit stands that once.

permit

Using this Maneuver lets the creature you target make one Move now, outside its Opportunity (0.24.0; rulings 239 to 244). Made by [EFFECT PERMIT: ...] on a Maneuver's own row, from the Human's Move Together (Mike, 2026-11-14): "You Move up to your Speed. The chosen ally may then spend ❶ of its own actions to immediately Move up to its Speed as part of this same Maneuver. It must finish adjacent to you." Through 0.23.1 the ally's drag on your Opportunity waited for the GM, as any Maneuver outside an Opportunity does. The word is Mike's choice: a permit is what the GM's Approve gives a player off-turn, and this is the same thing given by a Maneuver.

[EFFECT PERMIT: <what>; FOR: <who> [<N>]; LIMIT: round | encounter; IF: RANK(...)]

[EFFECT PERMIT: move; FOR: allies 0; LIMIT: round]                          Move Together ❶
  • One descriptor, what is permitted: move, the one word in this version.
  • **FOR:** is required and says who may be permitted and how near, in the words the grammar already has: allies, enemies or all, with a range in feet. FOR: allies 0 is an adjacent ally, as Steady the Line writes it. self and self+allies are refused: nobody needs leave at their own Opportunity.
  • **LIMIT: round** (or encounter) is the Maneuver's Frequency. A Talent's ALTER: <Maneuver>.limit replaces it (0.25.0; see alter).
  • **IF: RANK(...)** reads the owner's rank. RANK(roll ...) is refused: there is no roll.

Written on a Maneuver's own row and nowhere else, as GIVE is. Refused by name: UNTIL, VALUE, IF: CLAIM(...), IF: RESULT(...), IF: EFFECT(...), every condition about the other party, and a PERMIT after the ring of an [AURA ...] block.

As read: lets an adjacent ally you target make one Move now, outside its Opportunity, once a round.

In play, in an encounter:

  • Used with one creature targeted. The Maneuver's row shows the Use control. Refused, with nothing paid: nobody targeted, yourself, a target who is not one the FOR names, and a second use within the LIMIT. Warned on the card, and it still happens (Mike: "Warn and go on"): a target farther than the FOR range, with no action left, unconscious or dying, or not in the encounter. Tokens that look adjacent are sometimes a foot apart.
  • You pay at the click (Mike's choice), on the Maneuver's own card. Your own next drag in that Opportunity is the Maneuver's Move, already paid: one Move's worth, so a longer drag pays for the rest.
  • The one permitted drags its token with no request to the GM, and pays for the Move from its own actions. The GM's own drag of that token counts as the Move too. One drag: any other Maneuver off-turn still asks the GM, and an approval the GM gave that fighter for something else is not used up.
  • A Move, however short (ruling 242): a drag made as part of the Maneuver is never a Step and never a Rush, so it can provoke an Intercept, and the one-Maneuver cap holds it to one Move. A fighter at Speed 0 still crawls. An ALTER of the Maneuver's movement to step (above) lets a drag within half Speed be a Step for both.
  • Where it ends. When the one permitted ends farther from you than the FOR range, its move's card says so (Move Together: "It must finish adjacent to you"). Said, not enforced.
  • It lasts the Opportunity it was used in. One record on the user names both tokens; it is taken off when that Opportunity ends (the turn moves on, forwards or back; a lone fighter steps to itself; the encounter ends). If the one permitted never moves, it pays nothing. Two fighters may permit the same ally in one Opportunity: it moves once for each.
  • You must be in the fight. With a Combat on screen that you are no part of, nothing is paid, recorded or limited, as outside an encounter. A permitted creature that is not a fighter in it is warned about on the card and its drag is free, as any drag of a token outside the tracker.
  • Outside an encounter nothing is paid, recorded or limited: the card only. With "Track the six-action round" off nothing is spent, and the Moves are still marked as made.
  • On / Skip / Off on the Effects tab: Off, the Maneuver permits nothing (the click still pays, and so does the drag); Skip on the PERMIT line itself is read as On, as for every line that acts on use (a Skip on a Talent's ALTER of its movement is honoured; see alter).

subordinate

Using this Maneuver performs another Maneuver as part of it (0.25.0; rulings 245 to 251). Made by [EFFECT SUBORDINATE: ...] on a Maneuver's own row. The rule behind it is Mike's (2026-11-15): "any time a maneuver says to perform another maneuver as part of it, it is at the original maneuver's listed cost (i.e. costs 0 additional actions) unless otherwise specified" (section 3, the Subordinate Maneuver rule). The first row is the Human's Pay It Forward ⓿ (his draft): "Requirements You are acting at your own Opportunity and have just finished a check that consumed a beneficial Aid result from another creature. Effect Immediately after that check resolves, Aid one other willing ally as a ⓿ Maneuver. Make the normal Aid check and meet its normal requirements. You cannot target yourself."

[EFFECT SUBORDINATE: <Maneuver>; IF: EFFECT(<name>, used); LIMIT: round | encounter; IF: RANK(...)]

[EFFECT SUBORDINATE: Aid; IF: EFFECT(Aid, used); LIMIT: encounter]          Pay It Forward ⓿
  • One descriptor, the Maneuver performed, by the name the action sheets print. A Constellation and the row's own Maneuver are refused.
  • **IF: EFFECT(<name>, used)** is the trigger, when the row has one (section 3, Named Effect): a roll of yours at your own Opportunity, still running, has used up a bonus another creature's Maneuver of that name gave you. A row with no trigger is performed whenever it is used.
  • **LIMIT: encounter** (or round) is the Maneuver's Frequency, which a Talent's ALTER: <Maneuver>.limit replaces (Reciprocal Effort).
  • **IF: RANK(...)** reads the owner's rank. RANK(roll ...) is refused: the row has no roll of its own.

Written on a Maneuver's own row and nowhere else, as GIVE and PERMIT are. Refused by name: FOR, UNTIL, VALUE, IF: CLAIM(...), IF: RESULT(...), every condition about the other party, and a SUBORDINATE after the ring of an [AURA ...] block.

As read: performs Aid as part of this Maneuver, at this Maneuver's own cost, once a roll of yours at this Opportunity has used up Aid, once an encounter.

In play, in an encounter:

  • Two doors, one path (ruling 251). The Maneuver's row shows the Use control, and the card of the roll that used the bonus up shows a button for the roller's owner and the GM ("Pay It Forward ⓿: Aid"), on a check's card, a Strike's or a Cast's, or a Defense roll's. Only the card of the roll that used THAT bonus up shows it: an older card that used another Aid does not. The button does what the row does, and it goes when the Maneuver is used or the Opportunity ends. A Strike at three defenders posts three cards and three buttons; the limit refuses the rest.
  • What is performed is the subordinate Maneuver's own use (ruling 246): for Aid, the Relevant Check picker, the roll dialog with whatever your Talents put on an Aid (Cooperative Instinct's swap, Humanity's bonus), and Aid's card with its Give button. The card says "As part of Pay It Forward ⓿". Pay It Forward posts no card of its own.
  • The cost is this row's and never the subordinate's (ruling 245): Aid's ❶ is not charged. A row that printed ❷ would pay ❷, once, when the subordinate's roll is made.
  • Nothing is spent until that roll is made. A roll dialog that is closed has paid nothing, has not used the limit and has left the used Effect where it was. Once rolled, the limit is filed and the used Effect is spent: one bonus used, one Pay It Forward.
  • Refused, with a notice (Mike: "Refuse"): the trigger does not hold (no roll of yours at this Opportunity used up another creature's bonus; a result you still carry does not count), a second use within the limit, and a rank the line asks for that you have not reached. Off-turn the refusal comes first: the GM is not asked for leave the Maneuver could not use.
  • "Immediately after that check" is read as the rest of that Opportunity (ruling 248): the system cannot tell what else was done in between.
  • Who is Aided is chosen on Aid's own card, as for any Aid. You cannot pick yourself; you may pick the creature whose Aid you used (Mike: "Anyone but you").
  • Outside an encounter, and in a Combat you are no part of, the Maneuver is performed and nothing is asked or counted. No button is offered there.
  • On / Skip / Off on the Effects tab: Off, the click only shows the Maneuver's card; Skip on the SUBORDINATE line itself is read as On, as for every line that acts on use.

What this version does not perform, each told so with nothing spent: a subordinate that is a built-in (Recenter, Raise a Shield, the visor, Pass), one the system pays another way (a Strike, a Cast, a Move, a Step, a Leap), a parent row whose own cost is three or more (it would be Prepared), a second SUBORDINATE line on one row, and a subordinate that names a subordinate of its own.

requires

What a Maneuver needs before it can be used (0.28.0; rulings 281 to 289). Mike, of the Maneuvers tab: "I would like to only show Maneuvers that the system detects are applicable ... if you are not Prone or Supine, you cannot Stand. If you have no Spells, you cannot Cast. If nobody is within your reach, you cannot Grapple." A Maneuver's Requirements column is prose, which nothing can check; a [REQUIRES ...] block says the part of it a machine can.

[REQUIRES <condition> or <condition> ...]

[REQUIRES prone or supine]                                     Stand, Kip Up
[REQUIRES free hand or weapon grapple][REQUIRES creature in reach]  Grapple
[REQUIRES grabbed or restrained]                               Escape
[REQUIRES not prone]                                           Drop Prone
  • Where. On a Maneuver's own row (an action sheet's Automation cell), and nowhere else: on a Talent or a custom effect it is refused. A Maneuver a Talent grants is a copy of its row, so it carries the block too. It sits beside the row's other blocks, on the same line or its own.
  • Every block must hold. [REQUIRES free hand or weapon grapple][REQUIRES creature in reach] is "a free hand or a Grapple weapon, AND somebody in reach".
  • **or gives alternatives** inside one block. There is no and and no comma: a condition that must also hold is a second block.
  • **not turns one word round:** not prone, not controlling, not foe adjacent.

The words:

wordtrue when
a Condition's name: prone, grabbed, restrained, hidden, undetected, off-guard, controlling, controlled, bound, ...the character has that Condition. Spaces, hyphens and case do not matter
supineaccepted now, and never true until Supine is built, so [REQUIRES prone or supine] can be written once
bindthe character is in a Bind, of any kind (bound is the neutral Bind alone)
spellthe character owns a spell
shield, shield raiseda shield is in hand; it is in hand and Raised
rigida rigid implement is in hand: a weapon that is neither Flexible nor a natural weapon, or a shield
free handa hand is free. An estimate: a weapon or a shield in hand is a hand (two for a weapon held in two, none for a natural weapon), and gear marked In hand is probably one. When the system cannot tell, the row is shown
holdinganything is in hand
weapon, melee weapon, ranged weapona weapon is in hand, of that kind
weapon <trait>, melee weapon <trait>a weapon in hand carries the trait, matched on the trait's first word: weapon reload, weapon thrown, weapon grapple, weapon trip, weapon disarm, weapon shove
foe adjacent, ally adjacent, creature adjacentsuch a token touches the character's on the map
foe in reach (ally, creature)such a token is within the character's reach
foe within 30 (ally, creature; any number of feet)such a token is within that many feet, edge to edge
encounterthe character is a fighter in a running encounter

foe is a token of the opposite disposition, ally one of the same, creature any other token. enemy, enemies, foes, allies and creatures read the same.

The system hides a row only when it knows. Each word is true, false, or cannot be told: the character's token is not on the map, a hand the system is unsure of. A block fails only when every alternative in it is known false; anything it cannot tell leaves the row listed. A token the character cannot see is not counted (a wall between the two tokens, or the Hidden or Undetected Condition on the other), and neither is a token hidden from the players, a dead body or a party token; so a hidden foe never makes Grapple appear. Nothing asks who is looking at the sheet: the GM's copy lists what the player's does. "In reach" is the longer of the character's own reach and the reach of what is in hand.

It decides what is listed, and refuses nothing. The block is read by the Maneuvers tab alone (section 7). A player who shows every Maneuver may still use one whose block fails; no roll, cost or card reads it. The sheet's As read list says needs: Prone or Supine.

The Maneuvers the system itself runs need no block: Cast (spell), Close (controlling), Gain Control (bind, and not controlling), Raise a Shield (shield) and Pass (encounter) carry theirs in code. A [REQUIRES ...] block in such a row's cell replaces the built-in one.

Not read, and the table's: Size limits ("no more than one Size larger"), cover and concealment, tools and supplies, mounts and animals, "can hear you", "willing", what a Reaction's Trigger needs, and anything about the creature TARGETED rather than who is near.

grant

Talent Points at creation: [POINT ...] by scope, [<Constellation> trained] directed at one Root.

aura

The ring on the map, [AURA ...]. A drawing: what happens inside it is the Talent's other lines.
